newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Dec 31.

text.p: -- Iomega Corp said it will take a $10 million charge to cut between 500 and 700 jobs at its Roy, Utah, plant, increase production at its plant in Penang, Malaysia, and relocate its European headquarters.
The stock closed off 7/8 on Monday to 16-1/2 and touched a new year low of 16-1/4 during intraday trading.

-- Sandisk Corp, a maker of data storage products using flash memory, said it expects fourth quarter product gross margins to fall below those of the third quarter, while sales should be about flat with the third quarter's $26 million.
-- American Eagle Outfitters said it expects fourth quarter earnings to disappoint Wall Street due to flagging December sales.

-- Columbus Energy Corp said it could not account for the recent weakness in its share price and said it expects to meet forecasts for fiscal 1996 with earnings per share of about $0.60. Shares closed at 9-1/4.

-- Deluxe Corp sees fourth quarter pretax charges of $140-$150 million to complete a restructuring. It said earnings before adjustments should be about $0.50 a share for the quarter and $1.85 for the full year. Shares closed at 32-5/8.

-- Genentech Inc said it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market Nutropin human growth hormone for treatment of growth failure associated with Turner syndrome. Shares closed at 53-3/4.
